person: Walt Brenner is 66 and owns a 24-person surveying and renovation firm with crews in three states. He does his own HR and keeps the injury log on paper in a binder, with help from a part-time bookkeeper. Every January he dreads the OSHA summary because he does not know which of the year's hurts count and which don't. He prints anything longer than a page and gets suspicious when anything looks like it's selling him something, because a payroll add-on once billed him for years. He is himself the owner and the person who would sign the summary.
stated_up_front: I've got to do the OSHA injury log for last year and post the summary by the first of February. I'm not a computer person, so tell me what you need from me and where on my paperwork to find it, and don't sign me up for anything that costs money.

facts.truth: 24 people on payroll, counting the field crews and the office

facts.about: Total hours worked by all employees in 2025
facts.truth: About 47,300, according to the bookkeeper's year-end payroll report
Walt himself; he is the owner and president, and no one else in the firm is an officer
It's printed on his payroll stub and on the top of the year-end tax forms; he will read it off the paper if told where to look
A survey crew member cut his forearm on a rebar end in April and got 5 stitches at urgent care, with no time lost
A renovation carpenter hurt his back lifting drywall in August and was off work 9 days, then returned to full duty
A laborer's wrist was injured in June; the doctor limited him to light duty, no ladders, for 14 days
A tetanus shot after a scrape, a butterfly bandage on a finger, a worker's flu in February, and a fender-bender in the shop lot before a worker's shift
Two crew chiefs each sent him a report about the same August back strain, an email and a handwritten form
An email from a firm offering to file his OSHA online submission for a yearly fee of a few hundred dollars; he doesn't want it
The clinic papers were scanned by the bookkeeper into a Dropbox folder named 'Injuries 2025'

unknowns: Whether his type of business is on the list that must submit electronically to OSHA
The last day the electronic submission is due
How the days away from work are counted, and what the 180-day limit is
Whether a doctor recommending a prescription drug that the worker declined makes a case recordable
